packs.title: Hills, Art and River
packs.promise: Explore Napa through separate landscape, art and history outings.

q.s: Compare two open trail habitats without a long climb.
st: Use the posted trail map to choose a short open segment near the Browns Valley Road entrance.
Notice one oak-grove feature and one meadow or view feature without collecting plants.
Record a grounded comparison of shade, ground cover or sightline at the two points.

q.s: Compare recreation on land with the river corridor.
st: Choose an open path where a land recreation area and river-side edge can both be seen safely.
Record one design feature that supports activity on land and one that keeps water access controlled.
Write a short comparison of these two park uses without entering the launch or river.

q.s: Read one local-history source with its context intact.
st: Choose one credited source in an open exhibit or on the society's official website.
Record its date, maker or institution when given, and distinguish the object from the museum's interpretation.
Write one careful question the source raises without inventing a person's words or motives.

packs.title: First Street to Oxbow
packs.promise: Walk downtown Napa's civic spaces, river edge and Oxbow habitats.

q.s: Choose a downtown route from a current local source.
st: Find a current official downtown map or visitor display and locate First Street and the river.
Choose one safe public crossing for a later walk and record why the map makes it legible.
Draw a two-stop route note that distinguishes a mapped path from any unverified shortcut.

q.s: Read a civic park's layout with respect.
st: From an open path, notice how trees, seating or an amphitheater area shape movement toward the river.
Use the city's park plan to identify one designed public-space feature.
Write a respectful two-part note about gathering and quiet circulation, avoiding personal memorial details.

q.s: Compare one culinary object with its described use.
st: Choose one credited culinary tool or object in an open exhibit or official CIA source.
Record one visible material or shape and one use stated by the source; do not handle the object.
Sketch how that design might support the stated task, marking any inference as your own.
